outgoingFlows.description: Generation of new infections from existing infectious individuals. The number of new infections is modelled as the product of the time-varying reproduction number (R_t) with a discrete convolution of the previous infections, weighted by the serial interval distribution.

parameters.name: R_t
parameters.description: Time-varying reproduction number, modelled as a piecewise constant function that changes when an intervention occurs.

parameters.name: Initial R_t
parameters.description: Initial reproduction number before interventions, averaged across all countries (95% credible interval: 2.4–5.6).

parameters.name: Serial Interval Distribution
parameters.description: Distribution of the time between successive cases in a chain of transmission. Used to approximate the generation time distribution.

parameters.name: Infection Fatality Ratio
parameters.description: Population-averaged infection fatality ratio, adjusted for the age structure and contact patterns of each country. Based on previous work.

parameters.name: Infection-to-death distribution
parameters.description: Time lag distribution from infection to death, derived from assumptions about infection-to-symptom and symptom-to-death distributions.

parameters.name: Lockdown effect
parameters.description: The relative reduction in the reproduction number attributed to a lockdown intervention (95% credible interval: 75-87%).

uncertainty_analysis.methodologyNotes: This task is **parameter uncertainty quantification**: documenting uncertainty about **numerical parameter values** in the .compmodel (not structural or stochastic uncertainty). Confidence is **mostly Unknown** unless a small built-in heuristic matches the disease name (COVID-19, Malaria, HIV) and parameter name substrings — assigning High/Medium/Low requires curated literature ranges or expert review; see Phase 1 README (Validity & limitations).
